_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); cruise-line signals

pit_profile.why: Royal Caribbean: 'We are the world’s second largest cruise company operating 40 ships in the cruise vacation industry with an aggregate of approximately 92,300 berths as of December 31, 2010'; 'We compete principally on the basis of innovation and quality of ships, quality of service, variety of itineraries, choice of destinations and price'; 'We may lose business to competitors throughout the vacation market'; and 'The demand for cruises is affected by international, national and local economic and business conditions and is sensitive to reductions in discretionary consumer spending' (its own FY2010 10-K): a cruise-fleet franchise whose demand follows the economies it sells into, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: Royal Caribbean: 'We are the world’s second largest cruise company operating 40 ships in the cruise vacation industry with an aggregate of approximately 92,300 berths as of December 31, 2010'; 'We compete principally on the basis of innovation and quality of ships, quality of service, variety of itineraries, choice of destinations and price'; 'We may lose business to competitors throughout the vacation market'; and 'The demand for cruises is affected by international, national and local economic and business conditions and is sensitive to reductions in discretionary consumer spending' (its own FY2010 10-K): a cruise-fleet franchise whose demand follows the economies it sells into, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 2.20x; +51% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.05; conservative 2yr +18%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -73.5%/yr (worst year FY01-FY11, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +7.8%/yr (Q1 cc guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +7.8%/yr (FY01-FY11 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +97.5%/yr (best 2-yr run FY01-FY11); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: RCL (retrospective, 2012-02-24) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.20x (96.5% downside to Bear $1 / +43.9% upside to Bull $41) | Adj composite 2.19 vs market 2.14: gap +0.05 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +51% above the EPP floor $19 (9x FY12E $2.10) | Conservative 2-yr case: +18.5% total (+9.2%/yr) | At 13.6x FY12E the 15% hurdle price $38 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; Net Yields +3.2% in Q4 2011, forward net revenue +7.63-9.68% (Q1 2012 net revenue guide at constant currency); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
